# Quick start

The whole workflow for human RNA-seq samples takes four steps. Each function is
described in more detail in the rest of this vignette.

```{r quickstart, eval = FALSE}
library(rmskProfiler)

# 1. Build the index (once per species). This downloads GENCODE v48, extracts
#    the unique RepeatMasker TE sequences, annotates them, and builds a Salmon
#    index of transcripts + TEs with the genome as a decoy. Files are kept in
#    the rmskProfiler cache, the index is written to "hg38-salmon_index".
generateIndex("hg38-salmon_index", species = "Hs", threads = 12)

# 2. Quantify reads with Salmon using Gibbs sampling. This can also be done
#    outside of R (see "Quantifying reads")
salmonQuant(
    fq1 = c("sample1.R1.fq.gz", "sample2.R1.fq.gz"),
    fq2 = c("sample1.R2.fq.gz", "sample2.R2.fq.gz"),
    sample_names = c("sample1", "sample2"),
    index_dir = "hg38-salmon_index",
    out_dir = "quants",
    n_gibbs = 30,
    "--threads 12"
)

# 3. Import transcript and TE locus counts as an annotated
#    SummarizedExperiment, with counts scaled for multi-mapping uncertainty
se <- importQuants("quants", species = "Hs")

# 4. Sum transcripts to genes and TE loci to subfamilies
aggregated <- aggregateCounts(se, species = "Hs", te_level = "subfamily")

# Inspect, locate, or remove the cached files
listResources()
```

# Introduction

Transposable elements (TEs) make up nearly half of the human genome, but most
of their copies are similar enough that short reads cannot be assigned to them
unambiguously. `r Biocpkg("rmskProfiler")` quantifies TEs at the level of
individual loci from RNA-seq data by:

1. building a [Salmon](https://salmon.readthedocs.io) index from GENCODE
   transcripts, the unique sequences of RepeatMasker TE loci, and the genome as
   a decoy,
2. quantifying reads against this index with Gibbs sampling, and
3. importing the quantifications as a `SummarizedExperiment` with the
   overdispersion caused by multi-mapping reads removed, annotated with the
   genomic features each TE locus overlaps.

TE loci with identical sequences cannot be told apart by any read, so they are
collapsed into a single target named by the SHA1 hash of the sequence. The
annotation records all the loci (and their RepeatMasker classifications) that
share each hash.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("rmskProfiler")
```

Building the index and quantifying reads requires a recent version of
[Salmon](https://salmon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/building.html#binary-releases)
on your `PATH`. Importing and analysing quantifications does not.

# Index generation

`generateIndex()` runs the following steps, which can also be run on their
own:

- `downloadResources()` downloads the GENCODE genome, transcripts, and GTF.
- `rmskToBed()` filters the UCSC RepeatMasker annotations from
  `r Biocpkg("AnnotationHub")`. By default, records shorter than 32 bp and
  those with classes "Simple_repeat", "Low_complexity", "Satellite", "RNA",
  "rRNA", "snRNA", "scRNA", "srpRNA", "tRNA", and "Unknown" are removed.
- `extractUniqueSeqs()` extracts the sequence of each TE locus from the genome
  and collapses identical sequences.
- `createAnnotation()` annotates each unique sequence with the exons, introns,
  UTRs, and promoters its loci overlap.
- `createGentrome()` writes the gentrome and decoys and builds the Salmon
  index.

Downloaded and generated files are stored with `r Biocpkg("BiocFileCache")`
(see [Managing cached resources](#managing-cached-resources)).

# A worked example

The package includes example data for a 1 Mb region of hg38 chr22
(chr22:37,000,000-37,999,999): the GENCODE v48 annotations and transcripts of
the genes in the region, the RepeatMasker records in it, and Salmon quants of 6
simulated samples (3 "ctrl" and 3 "trt"). `exampleCache()` creates a temporary
cache containing the example data in place of the GENCODE downloads, so every
function can be run on it by passing the cache to the `cache` argument.

## Building the annotations

```{r load}
library(rmskProfiler)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
```

A [Salmon](https://salmon.readthedocs.io) index and all relevant annotation files can be constructed
with a call to `generateIndex()`. 

```{r build}
# Loads the example cache and files
bfc <- exampleCache()

# This GRanges object is only used in the vignette. keep rmsk = NULL in normal use 
rmsk <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "rmsk-chr22.rds",
    package = "rmskProfiler"
))

generateIndex(
    index_dir = tempfile("index"),
    species = "Hs",
    check_integrity = FALSE,
    create_index = FALSE,
    cache = bfc,
    rmsk = rmsk  # Set to NULL for normal use
)
```

With `create_index = TRUE` (the default) the Salmon index is also built in
`index_dir`. All other files (see [Managing cached resources](#managing-cached-resources)) are now 
in the cache:

```{r list}
listResources(cache = bfc)
```

## Quantifying reads

Reads can be quantified against the index with `salmonQuant()`, a thin wrapper
around `salmon quant` that runs each pair of FASTQ files with automatic library
type detection and the requested number of Gibbs samples. Any other Salmon
options are passed as character strings:

```{r salmonquant, eval = FALSE}
salmonQuant(
    fq1 = c("ctrl_1.R1.fq.gz", "trt_1.R1.fq.gz"),
    fq2 = c("ctrl_1.R2.fq.gz", "trt_1.R2.fq.gz"),
    sample_names = c("ctrl_1", "trt_1"),
    index_dir = "hg38-salmon_index",
    out_dir = "quants",
    n_gibbs = 30,
    "--gcBias",
    "--seqBias",
    "--threads 12"
)
```

Quantification does not need to be done in R. Salmon can be run directly, for
example on a cluster or as part of an existing pipeline, as long as:

- the index built by `generateIndex()` or `createGentrome()` is used,
- Gibbs samples are drawn (`--numGibbsSamples`, 30 is a good default), since
  `importQuants()` uses them to estimate the overdispersion from multi-mapping
  reads, and
- each sample is written to its own subdirectory of a common directory. The
  subdirectory names become the column names of the imported object.

```{bash salmon-cli, eval = FALSE}
salmon quant \
    -i hg38-salmon_index \
    -l A \
    -1 ctrl_1.R1.fq.gz \
    -2 ctrl_1.R2.fq.gz \
    --numGibbsSamples 30 \
    --gcBias \
    --seqBias \
    -p 12 \
    -o quants/ctrl_1
```

The example quants used below were created this way from simulated reads
against the index built from the example data (see
`inst/scripts/make-example-data.R`).

## Importing quants

`importQuants()` imports Salmon quants with Gibbs samples using a version of
`edgeR::catchSalmon()`. Each count is divided by the overdispersion estimated
from the Gibbs samples, which reflects the uncertainty from reads mapping to
more than one target. The `counts` assay contains these scaled counts, which
are suitable for differential expression analysis with
`r Biocpkg("edgeR")` or `r Biocpkg("limma")`. The `orig` assay contains the
original counts and `tpms` the TPMs.

```{r import}
se <- importQuants(exampleQuants(), species = "Hs", cache = bfc)
se
```

The `rowData` contains the annotation of transcripts and TEs. TE rows are named
by their hash and record their classification, the number of loci with that
sequence, and indicators for the features they overlap on the same strand
(e.g. `hasExonic`) or on either strand (e.g. `hasUnstrandedExonic`). The
`Ranges` column contains a `GRangesList` of the loci of each TE and the exons
of each transcript.

```{r rowdata}
rd <- rowData(se)
te <- rd[!is.na(rd$Hash), ]
head(te[, c("Subfamily", "Family", "Class", "N_Loci", "hasIntronic")])
te$Ranges[[1]]
```

## Working with SummarizedExperiment objects

`importQuants()` and `aggregateCounts()` return standard
`r Biocpkg("SummarizedExperiment")` objects, so the imported counts can be used
with any Bioconductor package or function that accepts a
`SummarizedExperiment`. Transcripts and TEs are rows like any other feature, so
they can be subset, combined with sample information in `colData`, and passed
on together:

```{r se}
colData(se)$group <- factor(sub("_.*", "", colnames(se)))
colData(se)

# Subset rows and columns as with any SummarizedExperiment
se[!is.na(rowData(se)$Hash), se$group == "trt"]
assay(se, "counts")[1:3, ]
```

For example, `r Biocpkg("edgeR")` creates a `DGEList` directly from the object,
keeping the annotation for transcripts and TEs, after which the usual edgeR or
limma-voom workflow applies.

```{r edger, eval = FALSE}
library(edgeR)

# Ranges is a GRangesList that would become a list column of GRanges in
# y$genes, so remove it from a copy of the object before converting
se_dge <- se
rowData(se_dge)$Ranges <- NULL
y <- SE2DGEList(se_dge)
keep <- filterByExpr(y, group = y$samples$group)
y <- normLibSizes(y[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE])
design <- model.matrix(~group, data = y$samples)
fit <- glmQLFit(y, design)
res <- glmQLFTest(fit, coef = 2)
topTags(res)
```

The `counts` assay is scaled for multi-mapping uncertainty and is not integer
valued. Methods that model the counts as negative binomial with non-integer
counts allowed, such as edgeR and limma, are appropriate.

## Filtering and aggregating

For many analyses it is useful to only keep TE loci with a single location in
the genome that do not overlap exons or UTRs on either strand, and to sum
counts to the gene and TE subfamily level:

```{r aggregate}
# subset() evaluates the conditions using the rowData columns. TEs have NA
# transcript_id and transcripts have NA Hash, so each row matches one condition
filtered <- subset(
    se,
    (!is.na(Hash) &
        !hasUnstrandedExonic &
        !hasUnstranded3UTR &
        !hasUnstranded5UTR &
        N_Loci == 1) |
        (!is.na(transcript_id) & gene_type == "protein_coding")
)

aggregated <- aggregateCounts(
    filtered,
    species = "Hs",
    te_level = "subfamily",
    cache = bfc
)

aggregated
```

# Managing cached resources

By default, files are stored in the rmskProfiler cache at
`tools::R_user_dir("rmskProfiler", which = "cache")`. A different cache can be
used by passing a path or a `BiocFileCache` object to the `cache` argument of
any function.

The cache holds three types of resources, as reported in the `type` column of
`listResources()`:

| Resource | Type | Created by | Contents | Approx. size (human) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `genome` | download | `downloadResources()` | GENCODE primary assembly genome fasta | 850 MB |
| `transcripts` | download | `downloadResources()` | GENCODE transcript sequences | 110 MB |
| `gtf` | download | `downloadResources()` | GENCODE annotation GTF | 65 MB |
| `annotation.txdb` | annotation | `createAnnotation()` | TxDb created from the GTF, re-used by `aggregateCounts()` | 200 MB |
| `rmsk.bed` | build | `rmskToBed()` | Filtered RepeatMasker records | 200 MB |
| `rmsk-unique.fa.gz` | build | `extractUniqueSeqs()` | Unique TE sequences, named by their SHA1 hash | 540 MB |
| `rmsk-duplicateInfo.rds` | build | `extractUniqueSeqs()` | Table mapping each hash to its TE loci | 150 MB |
| `rmsk-rowData.rds` | build | `createAnnotation()` | Transcript and TE annotations used as the `rowData` by `importQuants()` | 500 MB |
| `rmsk-gentrome.fa.gz` | build | `createGentrome()` | Transcripts, unique TEs, and genome used to build the Salmon index | 1.5 GB |
| `decoys.txt` | build | `createGentrome()` | Names of the decoy (genome) sequences | < 1 KB |

Downloads and the TxDb only depend on the species. Build resources also depend
on the `exclude` and `min_len` settings and are stored separately for each
combination of settings, identified by the `build` key in `listResources()`.
If you build the index with non-default settings, pass the same values to
`importQuants()`. The Salmon index itself is written to `index_dir` and is not
part of the cache.

```{r cache}
# Path to a cached file, e.g. to use it outside of rmskProfiler
getResource("gtf", species = "Hs", cache = bfc)

# Remove the files generated for the default build
removeResources(species = "Hs", cache = bfc)
listResources(cache = bfc)
```
